title: Inspire Test & Teach quiz package (itt.quiz.v1)
description: One complete, self-describing Test & Teach quiz: sections in teaching order, questions, correct answers, and a teaching explanation for every possible response. The Inspire Academic importer accepts any file that satisfies this schema and the additional rules listed in ITT_Quiz_Authoring_Standard_v1.md (unique ids, valid references, feedback that teaches). Order is given by position: sections are delivered in array order, and questions in the order they appear inside their section. Text fields are plain text; mathematics and chemistry are LaTeX between \( and \) (inline) or \[ and \] (display). HTML is never allowed.

objectives.description: The learning objectives this package teaches and assesses. Every question refers to at least one.

topics.description: The topics covered, e.g. one per line of the school's topic list.

assets.description: Optional images (diagrams, graphs), embedded in the file. Questions refer to them by id.

sections.description: The sections, in the order students work through them.

id.description: A short, stable identifier: letters, digits, dot, underscore, hyphen.

text.description: Plain text. LaTeX between \( \) or \[ \]. **bold** and blank-line paragraphs allowed. No HTML.

feedbackText.description: A teaching explanation shown to the student who gave this response. It must explain the reasoning in at least one full sentence; a bare verdict such as "Correct." is refused.

retries.description: How many times a student may try a question again after reading the feedback for a wrong or not-sure response. 0 means one attempt only. The first attempt is always kept.

id.description: Lower-case identifier that stays the same across revisions of this package, e.g. "y10-chem-structure-bonding".

source.description: Who or what wrote the package, e.g. "ChatGPT".

content_version.description: The author's version label, e.g. "1.0.0". Change it whenever the content changes.

data.description: The image bytes, base64-encoded, without a "data:" prefix. At most 400 KB per image and 3 MB per package. SVG must not contain scripts.

alt.description: A full description of the image for students who cannot see it.

type.description: The section's role. "mastery" marks an independent mastery check: one attempt per question, and its results are reported separately from teaching questions.

purpose.description: The intended learning purpose of the section, in a sentence.

requires.description: Ids of EARLIER sections that must be completed before this one opens. Omit for no gating.

questions.description: The questions, in the order students meet them.

id.description: Unique across the whole package, e.g. "s2-q07". Never reuse or renumber ids between revisions.

purpose.description: Optional. "mastery" is only allowed, and is implied, in a section of type "mastery".

not_sure.description: The platform adds an "I'm not sure" response to every question. This is the teaching explanation a student sees after choosing it.

teaching_note.description: A general explanation of the concept, shown in a supplementary panel once the question is settled.

worked_solution.description: The full method, shown once the question is settled.

options.description: 2 to 6 options, shown in this order. Do not include an "I'm not sure" option.

misconception.description: For a wrong option: a short label for the misconception it reveals.

answer.description: The id of the ONE correct option.
true or false, as a JSON boolean.

true.description: Shown to a student who answers True.

false.description: Shown to a student who answers False.

numeric.description: The student types a number. Marked exactly, or within the stated tolerance.

tolerance.description: absolute: within ±value of the answer. relative: within that fraction of the answer (0.02 = 2%). Omit for an exact answer.

unit.description: Shown beside the answer box. The student types the number only.

wrong_answers.description: Specific wrong numbers produced by known mistakes, each with its own explanation.

short_text.description: The student types a word or short phrase, marked against an explicit list. Ignores case, surrounding spaces and a final full stop.

accepted.description: Every exact answer that should be marked right.

correct.description: Shown for a right answer. Must explain why it is right.

incorrect.description: Shown for any wrong answer not listed in wrong_answers.
